notes: Settings journeys. These touch no model at all -- the panel reads and writes local settings -- so they are the cheapest deterministic coverage in the lane and the category had none. One covers what the panel presents; the other changes a value and reopens the panel to prove it stuck, which is the half a contents-only assertion cannot reach.

scenarios.name: The display settings panel names each control, its value and how to change it
scenarios.description: The display section of the settings panel -- asserts each display control is listed with its current value and its own description, and that the panel states how to toggle and apply
steps: waitForText:How would you like Kiro to display output?
verify: screen.contains:Spinners, progress bars, and loading effects
screen.contains:Decorative text art including table lines
screen.contains:Symbols for status, actions, and labels
scenarios.observe: Each control is asserted with its own description rather than its label alone, because the descriptions come from the panel's registry and cannot be echoed from anything the run typed -- a panel that listed labels over the wrong rows would still pass on labels. The three asserted controls are the ones that change how everything else in this lane renders: animations, ASCII art and icons. The toggle and apply hints are asserted because a settings list you cannot act on is only half the surface, and the toggle needle carries its arrow keys because the bare phrase also appears in a launch tip; the run gates on the panel's own question text, so none of these restate the wait.

scenarios.name: Toggling a display setting applies it and it survives reopening the panel
scenarios.description: One display control toggled, applied, and the panel reopened -- asserts the new value is what the panel reports afterwards and that the neighbouring control is untouched
steps: waitForText:How would you like Kiro to display output?
waitForText:How would you like Kiro to display output?
scenarios.observe: The value is asserted only after the panel has been applied and reopened, so the assertion can be satisfied by nothing except the setting having been written -- the in-panel change is never asserted, which keeps the predicate from restating a step. The neighbouring control is asserted still on because a toggle that wrote the whole section, or wrote the wrong row, would otherwise look identical to a correct one. Both needles carry their column spacing, which couples them to the table's layout: if the widths change, both fail together and loudly rather than one silently matching elsewhere.
